full_name: The Ritz-Carlton Penha Longa - Atlantic Course

summary.text: A 1992 Robert Trent Jones Jr. course in the Sintra hills, beside a monastery estate, which has hosted the Portuguese Open three times.

setting.text: Set in the southern foothills of the Sintra mountains, inside the Sintra-Cascais Natural Park, among valleys, hills and rocky outcrops.
The Atlantic course winds up and down the hills, with views of the coastal towns of Estoril and Cascais and the Atlantic.
The first three and last three holes sit in a wooded valley of pines and granite outcrops. The 6th to 13th are built on a hill with wide views.
Today's Golfer says the steep, sloping terrain gives stunning views, and calls the pink clubhouse and hotel unforgettable.
Top100golfcourses says it can be cold even in mid-summer, and that wind across the mountains makes it a real test.
The resort has a second layout, the nine-hole Monastery Course, also by Jones Jr., which opened in 1995.

history.text: The Atlantic Course opened in 1992, designed by Robert Trent Jones Jr.
The estate is the site of the first monastery of the Order of St Jerome, built in 1355.
Top100golfcourses says the name Penha Longa translates as 'long rock'.
The Portuguese Open (Open de Portugal) was played here in 1994 (Phillip Price), 1995 (Adam Hunter, after a playoff) and 2010 (Thomas Bjorn).
Bjorn won the 2010 Open de Portugal here on 265, 23 under par, five strokes clear of Richard Green.
Wikipedia says Penha Longa has also staged the Estoril Challenge de Portugal twice and the Estoril Open once.
The Ritz-Carlton resort hosted the 1999 Bilderberg Meeting.
The local church and Hieronymite convent date originally to the 14th century.

trivia.text: Top100golfcourses says the 1999 Estoril Open winner, Jean-Francois Remesy, was the only player under par, by two shots, when the wind blew.
Top100golfcourses says Penha Longa has 27 holes, a five-star hotel and 'not a single weak hole' on the Atlantic course.
The Ritz-Carlton says Penha Longa Golf Club was founded in 1992.
Golfbreaks says six of the Atlantic holes dip into the valley and the others play on the hills.
A Golfshake reviewer (August 2025) said the course feels like a rollercoaster, rewards position over length off the tee, and is walkable.

3.text: Lisbonpackage.com's course guide calls the 3rd and the 13th compact par fours that punish anyone reaching for too much club.

4.text: A Golfshake reviewer said a driver is safest left of centre on the 4th, leaving a shot to a green about 40 metres long.

5.text: The first par three on the course, played from an elevated tee that shows every hazard guarding the green, according to a Golfshake reviewer.

6.text: Top100golfcourses describes the 6th green as framed by a lake, with a medieval arched wall and castle tower behind.

7.text: A Golfshake reviewer described a par three with an aqueduct framing the left side and a lake all down the right.

8.text: A Golfshake reviewer called the par-five 8th a genuine three-shot hole, with cross bunkers at a variety of lengths.

15.text: Top100golfcourses says the par-three 15th needs a 155-metre carry over water and often plays into the prevailing wind.

16.text: Top100golfcourses calls the 16th the hardest hole on the course: a long drive across a valley, then a solid uphill approach to a narrow green.

local.text: The resort is at Linho, near Sintra, about a 30-minute drive from Lisbon.
Linho is an affluent village in the municipality of Sintra with a large expatriate community and the only American school in Portugal.
The Ritz-Carlton Penha Longa Resort was voted best resort in the Iberian Peninsula in 2018, according to Wikipedia.
